newsitem.title: USA: Lam Research sees rebound in June quarter.
newsitem.headline: Lam Research sees rebound in June quarter.

text.p: Lam Research Corp expects its business to begin rebounding during the June quarter as growth returns to the semiconductor equipment market, the company's chief executive officer said on Wednesday.
Before then, company and industry sales will likely reach a low point this winter, Lam's chief executive, Roger Emerick, told investors at a Montgomery Securities conference.

Lam still faces the loss of royalties in the quarter ending in March with the expiration of an agreement with Tokyo Electron Ltd, Emerick said later in an interview. That will lead to lower revenues than in the December quarter.
Looking further ahead, "We feel pretty good about the second half of 1997 as far as getting back into a growth mode," he said.
Emerick said Lam's orders suggest that forecasts for an industry rebound in late spring were accurate.
"We have booked well over $250 million this quarter," he said, describing that as "good news" that confirmed that the industry would break out of its current slump.
The semiconductor equipment industry began its decline last spring when computer chip makers curtailed expansion plans and cut back on equipment purchases.

As of 1995, Lam sales were growing at an annual rate of 75 percent, while the industry was growing about 60 percent. While Emerick demurred when asked if Lam expected to return to its former growth rate, he said he expected the company to continue to grow faster than the market as a whole.

Lam expects to increase its market share in etching equipment by two percentage points next year to 32 percent, he said. It expects to lift its share of the CVD equipment market to 10 percent from 4.0 percent currently.
